new.title: Capability manifest names a script that exists only in the task worktree, never git-added, so main lacks it and post-merge verify fails
new.cause: The implementer's working-tree file was never committed. Local runs see it, but main does not, so the manifest's script-check target ERRORs after merge. The gap is only caught post-merge by the capability-manifest tests.

verdict.severity_reason: The gap is caught after merge by the capability-manifest tests. That costs a failed verify and a rework cycle, but it is contained to tasks whose manifests name new scripts.
verdict.reason: The capability manifest plans/mcp-network-exposure-prd.capability-manifest.yaml still lists scripts/check_network_exposure.py as a script-check target. The script is neither tracked by git nor present in /home/leo/src/dark-factory/scripts, so a post-merge script check has nothing to run. The manifest itself marks the path as 'absent on main', so the missing file is observable. The 'never git-added' cause is not directly checkable, because the task worktree is gone from this view. The gap is only caught post-merge, because nothing in the tree compares worktree-untracked files against the manifest's script targets before merge.

new.title: Post-merge verify diagnostic harness unable to locate .task/ metadata files in task worktree
new.cause: When post-merge verification fails and the diagnostic agent attempts to reconstruct task execution state by reading .task/metadata.json and .task/iterations.jsonl from the original task worktree, these files don't exist (likely cleaned up after task completion or never synced to that location). The worktree is orphaned from its iteration metadata, breaking the post-merge diagnostics feedback loop.

verdict.severity_reason: Each sighting cost a few wasted reads during diagnosis. The agent can still diagnose from other evidence, and the layout itself is deliberate and documented in the PRD.
verdict.reason: In the current tree, `.task/metadata.json` is not expected to exist in a task worktree. `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/artifacts.py::ARTIFACT_ROOTS` routes `metadata.json` to the per-dispatch LANE root under `.task-meta/<lane>/`. `LANE_SYMLINKED_ARTIFACTS` exposes only `plan.json` and `iterations.jsonl` inside the lane's `.task/`. `iterations.jsonl` is a symlink into durable task storage, and the briefings say it is absent until the first iteration is logged. A diagnostic agent that reads `.task/metadata.json` will therefore always hit file-not-found. The `.task/` listing in the sighting (`plan.json`, `verify`, `reviews`, no `metadata.json`) matches this layout. I did not find any prompt in the tree that tells an agent to read `.task/metadata.json`, so I cannot name a specific file that teaches the wrong path. The post-merge diagnostic prompt may live in tooling outside this tree.

new.title: Agent constructs malformed Python one-liners in bash -c with improper statement separation
new.cause: When embedding Python code in `bash -c 'python3 -c ...'` commands, the agent concatenates multiple statements without proper separators (semicolons or newlines), causing Python IndentationError on parse

verdict.severity_reason: The error is loud and cheap to recover from: the script fails to parse and nothing partial runs. It costs the agent only a retry turn.
verdict.reason: The failure is still observable. The codebook at docs/legibility/confusion-codebook.yaml already holds many sightings of IndentationError from multi-statement `python -c` commands collapsed onto one line, so this cluster repeats a known pattern. The only Python-in-Bash guidance in the role preamble is orchestrator/src/orchestrator/agents/python_literal_guidance.py. It covers backslash escapes in pasted text and tells agents to use a quoted heredoc for scripts that carry pasted text. It does not say to avoid multi-statement `python -c` one-liners, and neither it nor harness_guidance.py states the general rule that statements need `;` or newlines. The cause of the missing separators sits in the model's generation, which I cannot verify from this tree.
verdict.proposal: Add a short rule that any multi-statement Python in Bash goes through a quoted heredoc (`python3 - <<'PY'`) rather than a `python -c` one-liner, because statements on one line need `;` or real newlines.

new.title: Orchestrated-task planning session abandons work mid-turn awaiting backgrounded task
new.cause: Agent launched a background task (run_in_background=true) but ended its turn before the task completed, or the harness reaped the task before completion, leaving work unfinished and no recovery path

verdict.severity_reason: The failure is detected and classified, and a retryable planning failure costs one lost architect run. The guidance is already in place.
verdict.reason: The failure is real and recurring. shared/src/shared/cli_invoke.py classifies it as AgentFailureKind.ENDED_AWAITING_BACKGROUND with the exact summary 'agent ended its turn awaiting a still-pending backgrounded task (work abandoned mid-turn)'. plans/agent-capacity-study-2026-09-09/S4-reify.md and plans/portfolio-review-2026-11-01/followups/model-routing-seats/U-unplannable.md cite it as 'architect failed (ended_awaiting_background)'. The architect role (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/agents/roles.py::ARCHITECT) already embeds BASH_CAPABLE_ROLE_PREAMBLE. That preamble (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/agents/harness_guidance.py) carries an explicit 'never end your turn while a backgrounded command is still running' rule and polling guidance. So the guard exists in the tree and the agents still occasionally ignore it. I found no remaining gap in an existing file that I can name.

new.title: MCP tool parameter contamination with XML envelope markup
new.cause: Agent serializes XML tags (</invoke>, </rationale>) from tool-call envelope into MCP parameter field values, causing systematic tool rejection

verdict.severity_reason: The guard already rejects the malformed calls, and the tool error recovers the actual parameters. The remaining cost is wasted retry turns, which is contained.
verdict.reason: The containment for this confusion is present in the tree. shared/src/shared/toolcall_markup.py, shared/src/shared/mcp_markup_middleware.py, orchestrator/src/orchestrator/mcp/plan_markup_stamp.py and fused-memory/src/fused_memory/server/markup_guard.py detect envelope markup such as '</invoke>' and '<parameter name=' and reject the call with error_type mcp_markup_detected. docs/mcp-toolcall-xml-leak.md and plans/toolcall-markup-containment-prd.md document the defect. docs/legibility/confusion-codebook.yaml already holds several entries for it, including add_design_decision with '</invoke>' or '</rationale>' in 'rationale' or 'decision' (around lines 3931, 3937, 22871 and 22900). Both sightings match that existing pattern, so the cluster is not novel. The cause is the model's own tool-call serialization, which this tree does not contain. No existing file here produces, teaches or fails to guard against it.

re_observed.title: Escalation watcher emits get_task_escalations calls with an empty-valued optional parameter (`"status": ,`), producing unparseable JSON that recurs across tasks
re_observed.cause: When the watcher wants to omit the optional status filter, it writes the key with no value instead of dropping it. The harness then rejects the whole call with InputValidationError, wasting a turn. The same malformed shape recurred for tasks 6060 and 5813, 63 turns apart, so nothing carries the lesson forward. The tool's parameter docs or the watcher prompt could state that optional filters must be omitted, not left blank.

re_observed.title: Interactive agent session with zero user turns contradicts session class
re_observed.cause: Session classified as 'interactive' but n_user_turns: 0 indicates no user engagement occurred; combined with early termination (size_bytes: 412) and single incomplete guard signal, suggests bootstrap/initialization failure or session-classification misattribution

verdict.severity_reason: It mislabels a few zero-signal, zero-turn digests in the sampler strata. They score 0.0, so the cost to the next change is contained.
verdict.reason: Verified in the current tree. `scripts/legibility/detectors.py::AgentClassEvidence.agent_class` returns UNKNOWN only when there are no records at all. When records exist and no marker matches, it falls through to `AgentClass.INTERACTIVE`. It never checks whether a primary user turn exists (`first_turn_text` stays None). `scripts/legibility/digest.py::render_digest` counts `n_user_turns` separately and takes `agent_class` as an input, so nothing reconciles the two. A transcript made only of assistant, system or isMeta records, or only sidechain records, therefore renders as `agent_class: interactive` with `n_user_turns: 0` and score 0.0. The `AgentClass` docstring says UNKNOWN is for an empty transcript, so INTERACTIVE is the unguarded catch-all. I did not check the two cited sessions' transcripts. I confirmed only that the code path can produce this output.
verdict.proposal: In AgentClassEvidence.agent_class, return AgentClass.UNKNOWN instead of INTERACTIVE when no marker matched and first_turn_text is None (no primary user turn was observed), and update the AgentClass docstring to say UNKNOWN covers sessions with no user turn.

re_observed.title: Digest 'User Corrections' bucket mislabels injected task context/briefing as a correction
re_observed.cause: Digest pipeline confuses task-instruction boilerplate (adjudication rubric, prior-round reference list, context) with actual user-provided feedback corrections

new.observation: The manifest at plans/mcp-network-exposure-prd.capability-manifest.yaml names scripts/check_network_exposure.py as a script-check target while itself marking that path 'absent on main', and the file is neither tracked nor present under scripts/. This rests on heuristic 10, clear invariants redundantly enforced: the invariant 'every manifest script target resolves on main' is checked at only one point, the post-merge capability-manifest tests, so a target that resolved only in the implementer's working tree reaches merge unchallenged. It also rests on heuristic 7, prefer stateless interactions between modules: the manifest's correctness depends on uncommitted working-tree state rather than on what the commit carries. The 'never git-added' step of the cause is consistent with the absent file but was not itself observed, since the worktree is gone from this view.

Two sessions read .task/metadata.json inside a task worktree and hit file-not-found. orchestrator/src/orchestrator/artifacts.py::ARTIFACT_ROOTS routes metadata.json to the per-dispatch lane root under .task-meta/<lane>/, and LANE_SYMLINKED_ARTIFACTS exposes only plan.json and iterations.jsonl in the lane's .task/, so the read fails by layout, not by cleanup or a missing sync; the brief's cause wording on that point is not supported by the tree. This rests on heuristic 11, SPOT: the layout has one home in ARTIFACT_ROOTS, yet the diagnosing agent's expectation of the path came from somewhere else, and no prompt in the tree teaching .task/metadata.json was found. It also rests on heuristic 13, files make internal sense in isolation: a worktree's .task/ listing cannot be interpreted without knowing the lane-root convention held in another module.

Both sessions produced IndentationError from multi-statement python -c one-liners whose statements lacked ';' or newlines, matching an already-populous codebook pattern. The only Python-in-Bash preamble guidance, orchestrator/src/orchestrator/agents/python_literal_guidance.py, addresses backslash escapes in pasted text and recommends a quoted heredoc only for that case. This rests on heuristic 6, well-defined purpose for each entity: the guidance module's purpose is literal escaping, and statement separation falls outside it, so no entity owns the rule. It also rests on heuristic 11, SPOT: the quoted-heredoc recipe exists in the repo CLAUDE.md anchoring section but is not the rule the role preamble states, so the lesson has two partial homes and neither names the separator requirement.

Two architect sessions ended their turn with a run_in_background task still pending; shared/src/shared/cli_invoke.py classifies this as AgentFailureKind.ENDED_AWAITING_BACKGROUND with an exact summary, and orchestrator/src/orchestrator/agents/harness_guidance.py already carries the 'never end your turn while a backgrounded command is still running' rule that the ARCHITECT role embeds via BASH_CAPABLE_ROLE_PREAMBLE. This rests on heuristic 10, clear invariants informatively, redundantly, uniformly enforced: the invariant is stated to the agent and detected after the fact, so the breach is named and recoverable, but there is no enforcement point between the two that prevents the turn from ending. It also rests on heuristic 11, SPOT: the rule has a single home in harness_guidance.py, which is what makes it possible to say the guard exists and was not followed, rather than that it was missing.

Both sessions carried '</invoke>' or '</rationale>' envelope markup inside MCP parameter values and were rejected with error_type mcp_markup_detected. shared/src/shared/toolcall_markup.py, shared/src/shared/mcp_markup_middleware.py, orchestrator/src/orchestrator/mcp/plan_markup_stamp.py and fused-memory/src/fused_memory/server/markup_guard.py all detect this shape, and docs/mcp-toolcall-xml-leak.md plus plans/toolcall-markup-containment-prd.md document it. This rests on heuristic 10, clear invariants informatively, redundantly, uniformly enforced: the rejection names the invariant via a single error_type, is applied at more than one boundary, and recovers the intended parameters, which is what contains the cost to retry turns. The leak originates in tool-call serialization outside this tree, so nothing here produces it; the finding records a contained recurrence of a known pattern rather than a gap.

phase_refinements.why: The manifest that names the script was authored during implementation, and the verdict observes that the manifest itself marks the target 'absent on main', so the defective artifact was produced in the implement phase; the stamp's 'unknown' origin is less precise than that evidence. The failure surfaced in the post-merge capability-manifest tests, which is the verify phase as stamped.

corrections.note: This run's verdict traced the output to scripts/legibility/detectors.py::AgentClassEvidence.agent_class, which returns UNKNOWN only for an empty record set and falls through to AgentClass.INTERACTIVE whenever no marker matches, without checking whether a primary user turn exists; scripts/legibility/digest.py::render_digest counts n_user_turns separately and never reconciles the two. The standing cause's alternative of a bootstrap or initialization failure is not what the code path shows, so the cause is narrowed to the classification fall-through. The two cited transcripts were not themselves read.
corrections.cause: AgentClassEvidence.agent_class treats INTERACTIVE as the unguarded catch-all: when records exist but no agent-class marker matches, it returns INTERACTIVE regardless of whether a primary user turn was observed, while render_digest derives n_user_turns independently. A transcript of only assistant, system, isMeta or sidechain records therefore renders as agent_class: interactive with n_user_turns: 0.

notes.claim: Four of this run's five new findings (fk-f9b718ee0766, fk-534838662cfc, fk-cef39957cd50 and, by its own verdict, fk-3335098ac5e9) describe recurrences for which a guard, classifier or documented layout already exists in the tree; only fk-656e5cc784ed names an enforcement gap. The pattern to weigh is agents not acting on standing guidance rather than missing guidance.
notes.evidence: Each verdict's reason cites the existing containment: python_literal_guidance.py and harness_guidance.py for the one-liner and background-task findings, the four markup-guard modules for the XML-envelope finding, and ARTIFACT_ROOTS for the .task/metadata.json finding.

notes.claim: The brief's cause text for fk-3335098ac5e9 ('likely cleaned up after task completion or never synced') is contradicted by its own verdict, which shows metadata.json is routed elsewhere by design; since the finding is new rather than re-observed, no correction was issued here and the created entry's cause should be read against that verdict.
notes.evidence: The verdict reason for fk-3335098ac5e9 in this brief, describing ARTIFACT_ROOTS and LANE_SYMLINKED_ARTIFACTS.

notes.claim: fk-282c6e761d54 gained three sessions this run with no verdict attached, which is the largest session gain in this brief for an open finding; the recurrence across tasks that its cause describes continues without a confirming or refuting read of the tree.
notes.evidence: The brief lists three gained_sessions and a null verdict for this key.

notes.claim: The brief reports 14 unkeyed re-observations alongside 3 keyed ones, so most of this run's recurrence evidence attached to no finding key and is not reflected in the observations above.

Verifier: The claim doesn't match the current tree. In scripts/legibility/digest.py, `iter_not_found` only collects not-found literals from tool_result content, and the output line `- (turn N) ...` is just the index of the matching record. The 'does not exist' text is ordinary tool output (for example a Read of a missing path) quoted from the transcript. It is not the digest reporting on turns outside the transcript bounds. I found no code that validates or reports on turn references beyond a session's range. The evidence reads like a miner misreading a not_found count (not_found: 2) alongside tiny session sizes, not a digest defect I can observe.
